newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau sees anti-Japan protests over islands.
newsitem.headline: Macau sees anti-Japan protests over islands.

text.p: Ethnic Chinese political groups in Macau staged angry anti-Japan street protests on Monday and demanded Japan's withdrawal from a disputed group of islands in the east China Sea which are also claimed by China and Taiwan.

The actions in the Portuguese-administered territory, which reverts to Beijing control in December 1999, were the latest in a wave of protests across the region over Japan's sovereignty claim to the Diaoyu Islands.

On Sunday, neighbouring Hong Kong saw its biggest anti-Japan rally on the issue so far when more than 3,000 people took to the streets shouting against "Japanese imperialism". Similar protest movements have been building up in China and Taiwan.
The Diaoyus, known as the Senkakus in Japanese, are about 300 km (190 miles) west of Japan's Okinawa island and 200 km (125 miles) east of Taiwan.
The dispute flared in July after Japanese rightists were found to have built a makeshift lighthouse on one of the islands.
About 200 protesters representing Chinese originating from China's Fujian province marched to Beijing's official mission in Macau territory and handed in a protest note.
The letter urged China to press for Japan's withdrawal from the islands, the demolition of the lighthouse and a public apology by Tokyo to the Chinese on the issue.
In a separate protest, members of a Macau liberal group marched to the mission with a letter asking Beijing to protect China's sovereignty over the islands.
Both groups are competing in Macau's legislative elections on September 22, the last such ballot before China takes back the territory of almost half a million people.
Other Macau political groups said they had sent similar letters supporting China against Japan in the islands dispute.
They said they might send protesters to Japan's consulate in Hong Kong, the Japanese diplomatic mission nearest to Macau.
Anger against Japan has been uniting Chinese in the British colony of Hong Kong, China and Taiwan.
